summary_paragraph: A 70-year-old woman with a history of CAD s/p CABG, hypertension, anxiety, and chronic back pain presented with worsening abdominal pain, nausea, and chills after being diagnosed with a suspected UTI in the ED. She developed hypotension requiring fluid resuscitation and norepinephrine, prompting ICU admission. Initial concerns for cardiac ischemia were ruled out with normal troponins and echocardiogram. Abdominal imaging showed chronic spine changes but no acute surgical cause. Chest imaging revealed mild pulmonary edema and crackles, leading to a diagnosis of community-acquired pneumonia, treated with levofloxacin. Her abdominal pain resolved, and labs showed transient anemia and thrombocytopenia that improved with treatment. Thyroid function tests suggested sick euthyroid syndrome. She stabilized, was weaned off pressors, and transitioned to oral antibiotics. Metoprolol was reduced due to hypotension. She was discharged home with instructions to complete antibiotics, monitor blood pressure, and follow up on thyroid function and mental health.
